findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a proving check for the comment-disposition ACs: e.g. grep the scope for the dead-narration phrases ('Ports ticket', 'byte-parity', 'Tier E', 'until E7') returning zero hits, a file-existence check that the ADR path exists in the tree, and confirm each named file:line no longer contains the stale claim.
evidence: AC9 is the only mechanized check: 'the full test suite AND make lint / make typecheck pass unchanged' — these prove behaviour, not comment content
AC3/AC4 disposition of ~16 docstrings and 6 named comments have no grep/file-existence proving check stated
AC8 'Any new ADR ... EXISTS and is committed' names no command to confirm existence
findings.finding: The comment-disposition ACs (dead bash-dispatcher narration relocated/deleted; individually-named stale comments corrected/deleted; ADR exists) have no explicit proving command — make lint / typecheck / the test suite cannot prove a docstring was actually dispositioned or that its recorded reason exists. Verification rests on unstated human diff review.
scenarios: A reviewer signs off believing all 16 narration docstrings were handled but a subset was silently missed with no grep to catch it
The ADR is referenced-then-collapsed but the ADR file was never actually committed
findings.suggested_fix: For AC3 add: `! grep -rEn 'Ports ticket-|byte-parity with the dispatcher|Tier E cutover|until E7' src/rebar/_commands src/rebar/_cli src/rebar/_engine_support src/rebar/_io`. For AC8 add: `test -f docs/adr/<explicit-init>.md` before any citing comment is collapsed.

findings.finding: The proposed new ADR 'Explicit init over silent-implicit tracker creation' restates a prior-art survey (git-bug/git-appraise vs git-issue/bugs-everywhere/Fossil) that ALREADY exists more fully in the repo, but the plan does not reference that existing document — risking a duplicate/divergent survey rather than a citation of the authoritative one.

scenarios: Author writes the ADR de novo and it drifts from docs/oss-comparison-and-remediation.md, leaving two divergent prior-art records
Reviewer of the ADR cannot tell the decision was already made and shipped, and re-litigates it

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the reads_cli.py 'collapse to one shared helper' item (AC5) with the parent's comment-only disposition contract — either reduce it to a comment-only disposition in this shard, or split the code helper-extraction out to a code-refactor ticket and confirm the parent sanctions it, so the leaf stays a subset of the parent's scope.
evidence: Parent 373f description: 'Each shard identified the real call-graph seam instead, and those splits are out of scope here.'
Parent disposition vocabulary enumerates only comment dispositions (RELOCATE/DELETE/KEEP/DO_NOT_MOVE/CORRECT-IN-PLACE) — no code-change class exists for a helper extraction.
Leaf's own headroom claims are careful to say 'WITHOUT any code extraction', signalling code extraction is treated as distinct from this shard's comment work.

Counter-evidence keeping this coached, not a hard contradiction: parent notes outbound_differ.py:164 had to 'buy its lines back from real duplication instead of from comments', acknowledging duplication-removal as a legitimate mechanism.
findings.finding: The leaf's AC5 mandates a behavior-preserving CODE change — collapsing reads_cli.py's five unknown-option blocks into one shared helper — which is a code refactor/helper extraction, not a comment disposition. The parent's contract is comment triage: its disposition vocabulary is comment-only (RELOCATE/DELETE/KEEP/DO_NOT_MOVE/CORRECT-IN-PLACE) with no code-change class, and it states the real call-graph seams/'splits are out of scope here.' The leaf thereby delivers work the parent's plan does not contain.
findings.location: Leaf superseding AC list, item: 'The `_engine_support/reads_cli.py` five near-identical unknown-option blocks are collapsed to one shared helper (behavior-preserving), verified by the existing CLI tests.' (and plan body: '`_engine_support/reads_cli.py` explains the same unknown-option rule in five near-identical blocks — a ->CODE fix (extract one helper) rather than a comment edit.')
scenarios: Implementer performs the helper extraction as part of this comment-triage shard, introducing a code refactor the parent scoped to comment dispositions only, which must then clear the parent's 'No behaviour change: full test suite AND make lint / make typecheck pass unchanged' gate.

findings.finding: AC3 'corrected where they document a live invariant, deleted only where obsolete' and AC4 'No load-bearing invariant is lost' rest on a correct-vs-delete judgment with no stated decision rule and no observable check; 'live/load-bearing invariant' is subjective as written, so the ACs are not deterministically evaluable.
findings.suggested_fix: Reframe AC4 as: 'For each deleted comment, the diff or PR note records why it is obsolete (referenced artifact deleted / superseded), so no comment documenting current runtime behavior is removed without a stated reason.'

findings.finding: The leaf's `_engine_support/reads_cli.py` item is a '->CODE fix (extract one helper)' — code refactoring/helper extraction — which steps outside the parent's comment-triage contract. The parent explicitly places code splits out of scope ('Each shard identified the real call-graph seam instead, and those splits are out of scope here') and its disposition vocabulary is comment-only (RELOCATE/DELETE/KEEP/DO_NOT_MOVE/CORRECT-IN-PLACE); a helper extraction also risks the parent's 'No behaviour change: the full test suite AND make lint / make typecheck pass unchanged' AC.
findings.location: Plan body: '`_engine_support/reads_cli.py` explains the same unknown-option rule in five near-identical blocks — a ->CODE fix (extract one helper) rather than a comment edit.'
